scope: Curated local-history and place reporting; no original 2026 probability model.
description: Additional independently sourced local context for selected congressional district guides. All other district guides render official Census geography, the election atlas and ACS data without invented places.

IA-01.title: The Mississippi River, a university town, and one of America's tightest House rematches.
IA-01.geography_deck: Twenty southeast Iowa counties connect the Iowa City area, the Iowa side of the Quad Cities, Mississippi River communities and farming towns stretching toward central Iowa.

character.title: Two different urban anchors
character.text: Iowa City's university-centered economy and Davenport's Quad Cities manufacturing-and-river economy give the district different local interests.

character.title: A river-and-rural coalition
character.text: Mississippi River towns coexist with agricultural counties, small manufacturers and central Iowa communities.

character.title: Do not confuse the 2020 boundaries
character.text: The district's current 20-county configuration began with the 2022 election. The candidate's six-vote 2020 win occurred in the old 2nd District, not today's IA-01.

county_results_2024.methodology: Official Iowa Secretary of State 2024 General Election county canvass for United States Representative District 1. Includes election day plus absentee votes; excludes write-ins and undervotes from two-party shares. All 20 county totals reconcile to the district's official 206,156 D and 206,955 R votes.

local_regions.title: The university corridor
local_regions.lead: The district's biggest Democratic voting center is also its academic and medical center.
local_regions.detail: The University of Iowa, its hospitals and clinics, and the surrounding education and healthcare workforce make Johnson County different from many nearby agricultural counties. Iowa City is also a literary and cultural center; Coralville and North Liberty add fast-growing communities within the same metro area. In 2024, Bohannan won Johnson County by more than 35,000 votes.
local_regions.why: Higher education, hospital employment, rental and housing costs, and the relationship between a college town and surrounding communities are central to understanding this part of the seat.

local_regions.title: The Quad Cities on the Mississippi
local_regions.lead: Manufacturing, river crossings, suburban growth and a close-fought county.
local_regions.detail: Davenport and Bettendorf form the Iowa side of a metropolitan area that also includes cities in Illinois. Deere, industrial suppliers, logistics and the defense economy shape the cross-river labor market. In 2024, Bohannan carried Scott County by 2,006 votes: the county was much more competitive than Johnson.
local_regions.why: A small shift in a populous, closely divided county can outweigh much larger percentage changes in a small rural county.

local_regions.title: The working Mississippi
local_regions.places: Clinton · Muscatine · Burlington · Fort Madison · Keokuk
local_regions.lead: Several distinct river towns, not a single political or economic community.
local_regions.detail: Clinton, Muscatine, Burlington and the Lee County cities of Fort Madison and Keokuk connect the district to the Mississippi River corridor. Manufacturing, shipping, local healthcare, river transportation and agriculture matter along this stretch. Muscatine is home to HNI Corporation and the headquarters of Stanley Consultants.
local_regions.why: The river counties are worth reading individually: Clinton's 2024 Republican margin was 1,673 votes, Muscatine's 1,010, Des Moines County's just 559, and Lee's 2,411.

local_regions.title: Factories and farmland farther inland
local_regions.lead: The district is also an industrial and agricultural interior, extending toward central Iowa.
local_regions.detail: Pella is home to Pella Corporation and Vermeer, major manufacturing employers in Marion County; nearby Newton, Oskaloosa and Indianola sit in a landscape of manufacturing communities, farming areas and regional college towns. The four counties of Marion, Jasper, Mahaska and Warren together contributed a Republican net margin of 16,718 votes in 2024.
local_regions.why: The industrial character of Pella and the Des Moines-area connections of parts of Warren County complicate any simple rural-versus-urban description.

local_regions.title: Fairfield and southeast Iowa's smaller communities
local_regions.lead: A cultural outlier and a much more Republican countryside.
local_regions.detail: Fairfield, the Jefferson County seat, is known for its arts community and Maharishi International University. It was one of only three district counties Bohannan carried in 2024, by 242 votes. Nearby rural counties voted quite differently: for example, Miller-Meeks carried Henry County by 2,403 votes and Van Buren County by 1,568.
local_regions.why: Jefferson demonstrates why county-by-county results are more informative than labeling the entire district 'rural' or 'conservative'.

explainer.headline: A college town, a factory belt, and a string of river cities
explainer.subheading: Iowa's 1st District is 20 counties spanning the Iowa City and Davenport areas, eastern river towns and the state's south-central manufacturing and farming communities.
explainer.reading: Start with Johnson County: Bohannan's advantage there was 35,222 votes. Scott and Jefferson added another 2,248 Democratic votes. Miller-Meeks won the other 17 counties by enough to overcome those advantages and win the whole district by 799. These are 2024 House results, not 2026 polling.
explainer.historical_note: 2022 and 2024 were fought on the same post-2021 district lines. In 2020 Miller-Meeks won a six-vote race in the then-2nd District; that is not the same map and should not be treated as a prior election in today's IA-01.

issue_lenses.description: Iowa City combines a major public university, teaching hospitals and a growing suburban corridor.
The Pella and Quad Cities economies include major manufacturers, suppliers and transport networks.
Burlington, Clinton, Muscatine and Keokuk anchor different stretches of the river and its industries.
The district reaches west and south into smaller county seats and farming areas.
